Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver

Class Desktop2DSplash

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.Desktop2DSplash
public final class Desktop2DSplash extends Object
A minimal start-up splash for the conventional 2D/Swing desktop, shown while the desktop shell is being built and disposed the moment it is on screen.

The 3D desktop has always shown the artwork splash driven by SplashStarter/SplashWindow (a full-bleed image plus a version and build-date caption). The 2D desktop showed nothing, so a cold start looked like a hang while the shell, the start menu and the restored session were assembled. This gives it an equivalent cue: an undecorated, always-on-top window carrying the product name, the resolved build version and - as a nod to the remote-viewing conceit behind the product's name - a "looking-glass" mirror in which the project mascot (the same icon the About window shows) is seen through the glass with a faded reflection beneath it. It never loads the artwork splash and never touches the 3D code path.

Like the rest of the desktop's dialogs, the content logic is split from the window assembly so it is unit-testable headless: resolveVersion(java.lang.String, java.lang.String), versionLine() and buildContent() construct only a JPanel (no top-level window), while show() and dispose() create and tear down the JWindow and are no-ops when the JVM is headless. The version is resolved the same way AboutInfo/AboutDialog do it - the "lg.version" system property (set by the Gradle run task and the release launcher) first, then the generated LgBuildInfo.getVersion(), then UNKNOWN_VERSION - so no version literal is hardcoded here and a bump cannot miss it.

    • show

      public static void show()
      Shows the splash, centred on screen and above every other window. Safe to call from any thread: the window is realised on the event dispatch thread and, when called off the EDT, this blocks until it is visible so the splash is on screen before the caller queues the (EDT-blocking) desktop build. A no-op when the JVM is headless, so CI and a display-less start never throw.

    • dispose

      public static void dispose()
      Hides and disposes the splash, if one is showing. Safe from any thread; a no-op when headless or when no splash is up.
